title: More Than a Bolo
author: Lexi Zotomayor
bodyText:
The wind outside had turned sharp, as it always does this time of year when winter begins creeping around the corners. Reluctantly waiting it out, I went to my bedroom to pass the afternoon on my desktop computer. There, an old *Philippine Magazine* article on the competition to design Andres Bonifacio’s monument caught my eye. I used to think neither design nor medium made much difference once a hero was gone. The details in those pages made me reconsider.

People tend to take monuments for granted once they are up. They stand in the middle of busy intersections like large stone punctuation marks, and we pass them thinking mostly about the traffic ahead. Looking through those pages reminded me that before a landmark becomes permanent, it begins on a drafting table as a set of competing proposals.

One detail from the record sets the history straight: Guillermo Tolentino won first prize with his tall shaft and cast of patriots, while Juan Nakpil placed second. Tolentino’s design rose thirty-five meters above the flat terrain of Kalaanan, telling the story plainly, from the heavy grief of oppression up through the gathered fury of the Katipunan to the winged figure at the top, so an ordinary passerby could read it without a guidebook. Closer reading also reminded me how easily public memory reduces a man to a single symbol. We picture Bonifacio almost solely with a bolo, forgetting he carried Mausers and Remingtons too, a detail Tolentino got right by placing both pistol and bolo in his hands. Even so, a contest only gives you a model on a table. It took three years, from 1930 to 1933, to turn that winning idea into bronze and stone.

A statue in bronze or stone can never quite measure up to a man’s devotion to setting his countrymen free, a devotion he paid for with his life. Yet seeing the thought and craft behind its design makes plain bronze feel like gold. It is an honest tribute to a sacrifice that earned him a rightful place among our heroes, remembered for far more than a bolo.
